standard_prerequisites.name: Root systems and sl_2-triple arguments in a finite-dimensional complex simple Lie algebra
standard_prerequisites.reference: Bourbaki, Lie Groups and Lie Algebras, Ch. IV-VI; the article's conventions at source lines 199-224
standard_prerequisites.use: Roots, coroots, the highest root theta and d_alpha = 2/(alpha|alpha) are assumed. The weight computation for (x^-_theta (x) t^{2k+1-i}) wbar, the vanishing of its x^+_alpha (x) 1 image via theta - alpha in R^+, and the resulting sl_2 conclusion are retained obligations.

standard_prerequisites.name: Garland's current-algebra identity, as quoted by the author

standard_prerequisites.use: The identity is quoted verbatim in the excerpt and is not re-proved. Its specialisation r = 2, s = 3k+1-i, alpha = theta and the subsequent manipulation of the resulting sum are the retained proof.

standard_prerequisites.name: Defining relations of the level-one Demazure module, obtained from the preceding source proposition
standard_prerequisites.reference: source lines 381-393 and 395-425, both supplied as context
standard_prerequisites.use: The excerpt carries the definition of D(1,lambda) and the author's presentation of D(1,k theta). The proof uses the resulting relations of D(1,(k+1)theta) at lines 489-490; nothing else about Demazure modules is assumed.

core_obligations: Part (1): show that v = (x^-_theta (x) t^{2k+1-i}) wbar_{(k+1)theta} has weight k theta and is killed by x^+_alpha (x) 1 for every alpha with (theta|alpha) = 1, using (theta-alpha) in R^+ and the relation (x^-_{theta-alpha} (x) t^{2k+1-i}) wbar = 0, and conclude from the sl_2-triple spanned by x^+_alpha (x) 1, x^-_alpha (x) 1, alpha^vee (x) 1 that (x^-_alpha (x) 1)^{k d_alpha + 1} v = 0 (source lines 469-476).

Part (2): apply Garland's identity with r = 2, s = 3k+1-i and alpha = theta to expand (x^-_theta (x) t^k)(x^-_theta (x) t^{2k+1-i}) wbar modulo the submodule generated by (x^-_theta (x) t^{2k+2-i}) wbar, then act on the resulting identity by x^+_{theta-alpha} and use the vanishing (x^-_alpha (x) t^r) wbar = 0 for r >= k+1 (lines 477-491).
Part (3): deduce (x^-_theta (x) t^{2k-i})(x^-_theta (x) t^{2k+1-i}) wbar in <(x^-_theta (x) t^{2k+2-i}) wbar> from part (2) of the quoted source lemma g (line 492).
proof_roadmap: Fix alpha with (theta|alpha) = 1, so that theta - alpha is again a positive root with (theta|theta-alpha) = 1.
Part (1): compute the weight of v and its annihilation by x^+_alpha (x) 1, then apply the standard sl_2 representation theory of the triple attached to alpha.
Part (2): specialise Garland's identity to r = 2, s = 3k+1-i, alpha = theta, use (x^-_theta (x) 1)^{3k+3-i} wbar = 0, act by x^+_{theta-alpha} and apply the vanishing relations of D(1,(k+1)theta).
Part (3): invoke part (2) of source lemma g.
difficulty_reason: The lemma is the technical core used later to build the map phi^- of the article's main theorem: it asserts three relations for the single shifted vector (x^-_theta (x) t^{2k+1-i}) wbar in D(1,(k+1)theta). Part (1) needs the weight computation, the annihilation by x^+_alpha (x) 1 through the root theta - alpha, and the standard sl_2 argument (source lines 469-476); part (2) requires specialising Garland's current-algebra identity to r = 2, s = 3k+1-i, alpha = theta, recognising that the resulting double sum can be grouped modulo the submodule generated by (x^-_theta (x) t^{2k+2-i}) wbar, and then acting by x^+_{theta-alpha} to convert the expansion into the claimed vanishing (lines 477-491). Neither the grouping of the Garland sum nor the use of the shifted vector's vanishing relations is a routine verification from the defining relations, and part (3) depends on a separate relation proved earlier in the article (line 492).
